name: Pawnee Pitch
description: Pawnee Pitch is a call-partner Pitch variant. Four players bid for trump; high bidder calls for a partner (by naming a card). Play follows standard Pitch: high, low, jack, game. First team to 10 points wins.

overview.description: Pawnee Pitch is a call-partner Pitch variant. Four players bid for trump; high bidder calls for a partner (by naming a card). Play follows standard Pitch: high, low, jack, game. First team to 10 points wins.

history.origins: Pitch descends from the English game All Fours (Seven Up), with bidding added; it became a North American family and social game, especially in the mid-west. Call-partner variants such as Pawnee Pitch allow the high bidder to name a card whose holder becomes their partner (identity hidden until that card is played). The Pawnee name is tied to a ten-point call-your-partner form; rules were contributed by James Adams, whose brothers learned it in Wichita, Kansas in the 1950s; the four-player, ten-point-to-win version is a common variant of that tradition.
timeline: See Pitch. Call-partner adds variable partnerships.
history.cultural: Part of Pitch/All Fours family; regional play in Kansas and mid-west USA.
history.evolution: Call-partner allows declarer to choose partner via card call.

rules.objective: First team to 10 points. Points: high (1), low (1), jack (1), game (1).
rules.gameplay: 1. Bidding: players bid 1-4 (or pass). 2. High bidder names trump and calls for partner (e.g. 'Ace of spades'). Holder of that card is partner (doesn't reveal until card played). 3. Play as Pitch: follow suit, trump. 4. Score high, low, jack, game for the bidding team.
keyRules: Call-partner: high bidder calls a card; holder is partner.
Standard Pitch scoring: high, low, jack, game.
Partner unknown until called card is played.

strategy.basic: As Pitch. Call a card you expect partner to hold.
strategy.intermediate: Bid according to trump strength. Partner inference.
strategy.advanced: Optimal card call; coordinate once partner known.
